question.problem:
The continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function $f(x)$ stated below. Given that $\text{E}[X]≈1.238\,10,$ compute $\text{Var}[X].$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}, & 0<x<1 \\ \frac{2{x}^{2}}{7}, & 1\le x<2, \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise.}\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ we can calculate the variance using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

 

We compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}],$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{2{x}^{2}}{7}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{2{x}^{4}}{7}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{{x}^{3}}{9}|}_{0}^{1}+{\frac{2{x}^{5}}{35}|}_{1}^{2} \\  & ≈1.882\,54\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & ≈1.882\,54-(1.238\,10)^{2} \\  & ≈0.35\end{aligned}
$$

 
rounded to $2$ decimal places.
